title: tenant-vpc-validation-lab-checklist-and-tf-migration-notes
content:
Purpose:
This working doc captures a lightweight, test-first validation lab and a companion set of Terraform module migration notes for customer tenant VPC onboarding. Intended for SRE and private-deployments engineers running field activation and upgrade rehearsals. The goal is to have a short checklist that teams can use during a customer kickoff to validate networking, security, and failover, plus concrete TF snippets and recommended migration guardrails.

Scope and audience:
- Applies to VPC-based private deployments (cloud VPC peering, Transit Gateway, or on-prem VPN/BGP).
- Audience: field eng, solutions, infra SRE, and customers' network teams.
- Not a full runbook for every edge case; use with customer README and tenancy contract.

High-level phases (timeline estimate):
1) Pre-kickoff (1-3 business days) - gather inventory, IP plan, contacts.
2) Validation lab (2-6 hours per tenant) - run checks in staging or customer test VLAN.
3) Terraform migration (1-3 days for simple tenants, incremental for complex).
4) Cutover & smoke (1-4 hours) - guarded rollout with rollback strategy.

Pre-kickoff checklist (must have before lab):
- Customer network owner contact + escalation path (name, email, pager).
- CIDR ranges for tenant VPCs (primary and reserved ranges), including allocation for pods/hosts and /32 exceptions.
- BGP ASNs and peer IPs where applicable.
- Egress inspection proxies / outbound allowlist requirements.
- KMS/HSM key IDs and cert rotation windows for on-prem.
- Expected peak RPS and latency SLOs for inference traffic.
- Maintenance windows and blackout dates.

Validation lab steps (executable, short):
1) IP reachability basic test
   - From customer side: ping/tcp to a pre-shared test endpoint in Redwood staging load-balancer on ports 443 and 10250 (for k8s health probes). Confirm both reachability and certificate chain.
   - From Redwood side: ping customer gateway IPs and BGP neighbor (if configured).
2) BGP session sanity (if using dynamic routing)
   - Verify BGP session established (show ip bgp summary) and advertised prefixes match agreed CIDRs.
   - Validate MED/LocalPref not overridden unexpectedly.
3) MTU and fragmentation check
   - Run iperf/mtr tests for MTU path, check for fragmentation on 1500 vs 9001. If fragmentation occurs, note application implications (gRPC vs HTTP).
4) Firewall and proxy acceptance
   - Confirm L7/L4 firewall rules allow SNI/TLS termination to our endpoint and allow egress to our storage endpoints if customer applies egress proxy.
5) DNS resolution and split-horizon
   - Validate customer resolvers can resolve internal platform hostnames when split-horizon is required; confirm TTLs.
6) TLS and cert validation
   - Exchange cert fingerprint and verify chain; confirm OCSP/CRL access if mutual TLS enforced.
7) Latency baseline
   - Generate 1k inference-style requests (sample payload) and record p50/p95 p99. Compare against expected SLO.
8) KV/prefix caching validation
   - For longer sessions, confirm KV cache warmup or prefix caching behavior matches expected token budget (example checks in lab appendix).
9) Observability hooks
   - Confirm traces and logs arrive at Redwood Console (or test collector), verify token-level attribution for sample request.
10) Failover simulation
   - Simulate primary region outage (route withdraw, BGP flap) and verify traffic fails over to secondary model variant or region according to policy. Time the RTO.

Acceptance criteria (gate for cutover):
- All reachability tests pass with no more than 1 intermittent failure in 30 tests.
- BGP sessions stable >= 5 minutes with consistent prefix set.
- End-to-end p99 latency within 2x the SLO during baseline load.
- Observability: sample traces attributed and logs show no TLS handshake failures.
- Security: egress allowlist and KMS integration validated in staging.

Rollback scenarios (quick decision tree):
- If TLS handshake failures persist after 3 remediation attempts -> rollback to customer-side routing to previous endpoint (instructions below).
- If p99 spikes >3x SLO for >15 minutes after cutover -> trigger traffic routing back to hosted fallback and open incident.
- BGP instability leading to prefix churn >5 withdraws in 10 minutes -> withdraw peering and fail closed to safe network (manual).

Quick rollback command examples (customer side):
- Remove route to redwood CIDR on transit: ip route delete 10.40.0.0/16 via 192.0.2.5
- On TGW, revert attachment: aws ec2 detach-transit-gateway-vpc-attachment --transit-gateway-attachment-id tgw-attach-abc123

Terraform module migration notes (principles):
- Keep state changes small: prefer one resource group per commit. Large module replacements should be done via terraform state mv and explicit import when necessary.
- Make network changes idempotent and reversible: add new TGW attachment and test before removing old peering.
- Use lifecycle ignore_changes for ephemeral fields (peer owner id, attachment state) to avoid unnecessary diffs.
- Encourage customers to apply TF in a tenant-namespaced workspace to reduce blast radius.

Suggested TF snippets (conceptual patterns):
- Transit Gateway attachment pattern (attach first, then route):

resource "aws_ec2_transit_gateway_vpc_attachment" "redwood_attach" {
  vpc_id = var.tenant_vpc_id
  subnet_ids = var.private_subnet_ids
  transit_gateway_id = var.redwood_tgw_id
  tags = { Name = "redwood-attach-${var.tenant_id}" }
}

resource "aws_route" "to_tgw" {
  for_each = toset(var.service_prefixes)
  route_table_id = var.private_route_table
  destination_cidr_block = each.value
  transit_gateway_id = var.redwood_tgw_id
}

Notes: attach resource first; do not delete old peering until routes validate. If using on-prem VPN, prefer static route entries for cutover window then enable BGP.

Terraform pitfalls observed in field:
- Implicit dependencies causing transient detach/attach: add explicit depends_on where needed.
- State drift from manual console edits: capture drift report and align before scripted migration.
- Large CIDR renames: avoid renaming ranges in-place — prefer add-and-deprecate flow with clear timeline.

Field-tested migration guardrails:
- Stepwise traffic switch: add new path, mirror traffic (sampling), then cutover 5-10% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% with checks at each stage.
- Maintain dual advertising in BGP for at least 10 minutes to validate path metrics.
- Use TTL=30 on DNS records for faster rollback; inform customer to keep low for first 48 hours.

Observability & metrics to collect during validation/cutover:
- p50/p95/p99 inference latency and success rate
- TLS handshake success rate and certificates rejected
- BGP adjacency up/down events and prefix count
- Packet loss and retransmit rates (iperf/mtr)
- Token cost per request (sanity check on billing accounting)

Known issues and mitigations (field notes):
- Issue: MTU drops cause gRPC streaming stalls. Mitigation: prefer jumbo frames where supported or enable path MTU discovery and reduce chunk size for streaming.
- Issue: Corporate firewalls drop long-lived connections. Mitigation: enable periodic keepalive and configure shorter TLS session lifetimes.
- Issue: Terraform state ownership conflicts between customer and Redwood. Mitigation: clear ownership model in contract; suggest using a cross-account S3 backend with enforced IAM roles.

Appendix A: simple test harness commands
- TCP connect check: curl -v --resolve "api.redwood-test.example:443:203.0.113.21" https://api.redwood-test.example/healthz
- BGP check (exabgp/tester): exabgpcli neighbor show | grep Established || echo "BGP DOWN"
- Latency load quick: hey -n 1000 -c 50 -m POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"prompt":"hi"}' https://api.redwood-test.example/v1/generate

Appendix B: Post-mortem starter template
- Incident summary (one-liner)
- Timeline of events with timestamps
- Root cause analysis (network / infra / config / TF)
- Actions taken and rollbacks performed
- Follow-ups (TF changes, runbook edits, automation tests)

Appendix C: Quick contact matrix (example)
- Redwood field lead: Aisha Patel (aisha@redwood.com)
- SRE on-call: Marcus Reed (pager)
- Customer network lead: <fill>

Next steps before release:
- Convert these validation checks into an automated checklist in Console ticketing.
- Add a small Terraform test workspace template in private-tf-modules repo.
- Run a cross-team dry run with Solutions + Customer Success on two upcoming customers.

End of draft.
